summary: Democrat Hannah Pingree has consistently led Republican Bobby Charles by double digits for the open governor's seat, with independent former GOP chair Rick Bennett on a narrow path, per the Portland Press Herald. The race turns on energy and housing costs, a projected 1 billion dollar budget gap, tariffs and the Iran war, with Charles tying Pingree to Gov. Janet Mills while distancing himself from Trump on tariffs, per the Bangor Daily News and Press Herald.

issues.why: Maine faces a projected 1.085 billion dollar gap, and Charles wants deep cuts and to phase out the income tax while Pingree would raise taxes on nonresident second homes.
Charles blames Pingree and Mills for high energy bills while Pingree ties rising fuel prices to the Iran war.
All three candidates agree Maine is building homes too slowly but differ on the fix.
Maine's economy is tied to Canada, and even Charles breaks with Trump on broad tariffs, calling Canada a friend.
The candidates agree Maine struggles to keep rural hospitals open and health care workers in the state.

storylines.title: Charles invites critics to grill him
storylines.what: Trailing in polls, Charles scheduled an open event in Auburn where Pingree supporters and Harris voters can challenge him.

storylines.title: Final debate leaves Pingree in front
storylines.what: At the WMTW debate Charles again called Pingree and Mills insiders, and Pingree said Bennett is a lifelong Republican, with no major moments.

storylines.title: GOP donor PAC boosts Bennett instead
storylines.what: A PAC formed by Republican donors to help Charles spent 70,000 dollars boosting Bennett, and promised RGA money for Charles has not appeared.

storylines.title: Budget gap plans laid out
storylines.what: Charles pledged to cut at least 1 billion dollars through fraud reduction and a hiring freeze, while Pingree proposed doubling the homestead exemption and taxing nonresident second homes.

storylines.title: Wabanaki chiefs back Pingree
storylines.what: Four Wabanaki chiefs endorsed Pingree after she pledged to sign tribal sovereignty legislation in her first 100 days.

storylines.title: Charles hits grant to Pingree's former nonprofit
storylines.what: In the Bangor debate Charles questioned an 840,000 dollar state award to a nonprofit Pingree once led and tied her to Mills.

storylines.title: First debate turns on Trump and the Iran war
storylines.what: Pingree tied rising prices to the Iran war and Trump, while Charles broke with Trump on the war and broad tariffs and attacked Pingree's record in Augusta.

events.title: Close the 1 billion dollar gap
events.prompt: Maine projects a gap of more than 1 billion dollars in the next budget. How do you close it?

opts.label: Tax second homes
opts.say: Raise taxes on nonresident second homes and double the homestead exemption for locals.

opts.label: Line by line review
opts.say: Form a bipartisan finance team and an inspector general to root out misspending.

opts.label: Cut 1 billion now
opts.say: Freeze hiring, cut 2,000 vacant jobs and start phasing out the income tax.

events.title: Tariffs on Canada
events.prompt: Broad federal tariffs are hitting trade with Canada, Maine's biggest partner. How do you respond?

opts.label: Fight the tariffs
opts.say: Call the tariffs a tax on Mainers and pledge to fight the administration.

opts.label: Targeted only
opts.say: Oppose broad tariffs on Canada while backing some targeted ones.

opts.label: Back the president
opts.say: Defend tariffs as leverage that will bring better deals for Maine.

events.title: Tribal sovereignty
events.prompt: Wabanaki leaders want full tribal sovereignty legislation signed early in the next term. Do you commit?

opts.label: Sign in 100 days
opts.say: Pledge to sign full sovereignty legislation in your first 100 days.

opts.label: Negotiate step by step
opts.say: Support talks on sovereignty issues one at a time.

opts.label: Decline to commit
opts.say: Avoid a commitment and focus on economic issues instead.

events.title: Running against Augusta
events.prompt: Your rival says you are part of the Mills insider machine that raised energy and housing costs. How do you answer?

opts.label: Own the record
opts.say: Defend Democratic leadership and blame Trump's war and tariffs for prices.

opts.label: Pitch independence
opts.say: Say both parties are a political industrial complex and promise compromise.

opts.label: Hammer the insiders
opts.say: Attack state grants and spending as insider deals and promise to clean house.
